chatMessages.text: Riya, tonight we're doing it. The Kottayam call. Full spreadsheet, EMI, everything. Ente amme is going to see the numbers and say 'aiyyo mole, so much debt.'

She might. And then she'll see the line at the top, the one you asked me to add — the remittance. Fifteen thousand, first position, before the EMI. Untouched. This call isn't asking permission, Jessy — it's sharing the architecture. And tell Amma four families from the parish are in the same project. She'll hear 'neighbourhood,' not 'debt.'

tabs.insightTitle: What I noticed while we were searching
tabs.insightDescription: “The Mathews are the Bengaluru that keeps the other Bengalurus alive — and they shop the way they work: pre-approval first, census second, and a nurse-scheme rate hunted at bank two for its −0.35%. Their diligence instrument is time-of-day — buildings auditioned at 10 am, when the water pumps and loudspeakers are actually speaking. And their architecture is the parish: four congregation families in one project settled community, school-van sharing, and Sunday logistics in a single conversation, which is what no portal has ever done. The remittance line sits before the EMI, always — the Kottayam call shared the spreadsheet, and Amma heard 'neighbourhood' instead of 'debt.' Love and expectations, same currency.”

differentlyCards.title: Ask about the nurse scheme at the first call
differentlyCards.description: The −0.35% was found at bank two in month one — asking about healthcare-worker schemes at every bank's first call would have surfaced it instantly.

differentlyCards.title: Run the 10 am audit from the first shortlist
differentlyCards.description: The loudspeaker tower survived two visits at 6 pm — the day-sleep audit should have been gate zero, not gate three.

differentlyCards.title: Ask the parish about projects before the census
differentlyCards.description: The four-family discovery arrived at month six — the congregation's housing knowledge would have accelerated the whole shortlist.

differentlyCards.title: Put the remittance line on the first budget page
differentlyCards.description: The line was always sacred — putting it literally first on page one would have ended the 'maybe with more shifts' weeks earlier.

chatMessages.text: Amma saw the remittance line first, the plan under it, four parish families around it — and then she blessed the spreadsheet. I think the house got blessed before the booking did.
That's the order it should always be: the people first, then the plan, then the walls. The 2 ams you work for this city bought you a Sunday morning — with Amma's blessing attached.

Jessy and Thomas proved the city's 2 ams can buy a Sunday morning — slab by slab, blessing included.
